persona.title: Pretend you are…
persona.text: Pretend you are Carol, 61. You make scented candles in your kitchen and sell them from a little shop downtown. You work hard every month, but at the end of the month there is almost nothing left. Today you want to know: how many candles must I sell before I stop losing money, and is my price too low?

challenge.intro: Now you are Carol with the candle shop. The app is empty. Nobody will tell you which button to press — use what you learned. When you finish, tap Check my work.
challenge.start: Open Break-Even. If the welcome tour shows, tap 'skip the tour' → '✨ Start fresh with my own' → OK. If it does not show, scroll to the very bottom of the page and tap '🧹 Start fresh — erase this app’s data' → OK → OK. The three boxes are now empty.

tasks.text: One candle costs you: wax $4, wick $1.50 and the jar $0.50. Put in what ONE candle costs you to make.
tasks.hint: Add the three costs for one candle together (4 + 1.50 + 0.50). It goes in the box for the cost of ONE sale, not the monthly box.

tasks.text: Every month you pay shop rent of $1,500 and utilities of $900. Put in your monthly costs.
tasks.hint: Rent and utilities are paid every month even if you sell nothing. Add them together and put the total in the monthly box.

tasks.text: You can sell about 15 candles a day — 450 a month — and customers will not pay more than $15. Set a price that covers all your costs with 450 sales a month or fewer.
tasks.hint: Look at 'Sales needed / month' as you change the price. It must be 450 or less, and the price must be 15 or less.

tasks.text: Find the LOWEST whole-dollar price that still covers all your costs with 450 sales a month. Leave that price in the app.
tasks.hint: Try prices one dollar at a time (11, 12, 13…) and watch 'Sales needed / month'. Pick the smallest price where it is 450 or less.

ownWords.question: In your own words, what is this app for?
keyIdeas: tells you how many sales you need before you stop losing money
uses your price, the cost of one item, and your monthly costs
lets you test a different price before you change it

lines: Welcome. This short video explains Break-Even. In about three and a half minutes you will know what it is for and how to use it.
First, the problem. Many small sellers choose a price by guessing. They copy the table next to them, or pick a round number.
Then they work hard all month, and at the end there is almost nothing left. And they do not know why.
The answer is usually hiding in three numbers. Break-Even asks for those three numbers and gives you one honest answer.
Who is it for? Anyone who sells something: candles at a craft fair, baked goods, a side business online. The math is the same.
The question at the top is the whole app: how many sales until you stop losing money?
Below it are three boxes. Box one is called Average price per sale. It is what a customer pays you for one, on average.
Box two is Variable cost per sale. What each one costs you: materials, packaging, shipping, card fees. It goes up when you sell more.
Box three is Monthly fixed costs. What you pay every month even if you sell nothing: rent, booth fees, software, insurance.
Be careful here. Rent is paid once a month, so it goes in box three. The wax in each candle is used on every sale, so it goes in box two.
As soon as you type, the answers appear below. There is no button to press, and your numbers save on this phone by themselves.
The first answer is Sales needed a month. This is the big one: the sale where you stop losing money.
Next to it, Revenue needed a month. How much money has to come in to cover everything.
You keep per sale is your price minus what each one costs. That is what pays your monthly bills.
And Margin percent: how many cents you keep out of each dollar a customer pays.
Let us try an example together. Say you make candles. You sell each one for ten dollars. The wax, wick and jar cost you four dollars. So you keep six dollars a candle.
Your craft-fair table costs fifty dollars a month, whether you sell or not. Fifty divided by six is a little over eight. So the answer is nine.
Sell nine candles a month and every cost is covered. From the tenth candle on, you are making money.
Now look at the table under the answers. It is called If your price were. It shows your price now, and ten or twenty percent lower and higher.
Each row shows the sales you would need at that price. At twelve dollars, only seven candles. At eight dollars, thirteen. Same work, very different month.
If your price is at or below what one costs you, a red message says so plainly: no number of sales will ever break even. The fix is to raise the price.
Below that is an optional extra: a Cash Flow Tracker spreadsheet that does this plus a twelve-month plan. You do not need it to use Break-Even.
How to start. Type your real price in box one, then what one costs you, then your monthly costs. Read the first answer out loud.
Then try a slightly higher price in the table and see what it does. That is how you pick a price on purpose instead of by guess.
Your numbers stay only on this phone. There is no account, and nothing is sent anywhere. To clear them, tap Start fresh at the very bottom. It asks you twice first.
Break-Even is free.
And the question mark button in the corner has the tour and help any time you need them.

daily.task: Try one new number in Break-Even (a new price or a new cost) and look at the answer.

explore.name: 🔢 The three boxes
explore.find: Open Break-Even. The boxes are at the top.
explore.try: Type a price, a cost and monthly costs. Then try: empty, 0, letters, a cost bigger than the price, and a huge number.

explore.name: 📊 The four answers
explore.try: Check all four numbers change as you type, and make sense.

explore.name: 📋 The price table
explore.try: Look at the five rows. The bold “Now” row should match box 1.

explore.name: 🔁 Come back later
explore.find: Close the tab, then open Break-Even again.

explore.name: 🛒 The offer box
explore.try: Read it. Tap it to see where it goes — don’t buy anything.

explore.name: ❓ The round ? button
explore.find: Tap the round ? in the bottom corner.
explore.try: Open every line in it: Aa (size), ✨ Ask an AI, 🌉 More from Daraja, 🎬 Take the tour again. Close it. Leave “Start fresh” for the very end.
